items.title: Reading Guide
items.text:
دليل القراءة ترتيب الميزات (Features)

الميزات في هذا الموقع مرتبة بنفس الترتيب الموجود في Obsidian، حتى يسهل الرجوع إليها والمقارنة بين المصدرين.

تقسيم صفحة كل Feature قرارات الفريق في نظام الترشيحات (Recommendation System)

في آخر صفحة كل ميزة من ميزات نظام الترشيحات، يوجد قسم قرارات الاجتماع (Meeting Decisions)، وفيه ما اتفق عليه الفريق بعد الاجتماع.

وبناءً على هذه القرارات، تم تعديل بعض أجزاء الميزات حتى تناسب احتياجات الفريق، مثل حذف الأسئلة التي تمت الإجابة عنها، وتعديل بعض المتطلبات.

قرارات ميزات الـ Agents

تم تحديد قرارات ميزات الـ Agents ونسبة أهمية كل ميزة بناءً على عاملين أساسيين:

  • التكلفة (Cost): المجهود والوقت المطلوبان لتنفيذ الميزة.
  • الفائدة للعملاء (Customer Value): الميزات التي تفيد العملاء بشكل أسرع حصلت على أهمية أعلى.
صفحة القرارات النهائية (Final Decisions)

تعرض صفحة القرارات النهائية كل الميزات مرتبة من الأكثر أهمية إلى الأقل أهمية، حتى يكون من السهل معرفة ما يجب البدء به.

items.title: Team Requests
items.text: This page lists problems and requests reported by the GoCare team in existing tools.

items.title: Product Codes Sheet
items.text: The team registers products in a sheet, using a code for each product. The team reported two problems:

items.title: 1. No alert for duplicate codes
items.text: The sheet should show an alert when the same product code is entered more than once, but this does not happen today. As a result, the same product can be registered twice without anyone noticing.

items.title: 2. Product sizes appear as separate products
items.text: When a product has more than one size, such as 40 ml and 90 ml, the website treats them as two different products, and each one appears in a different place.

items.title: What the team needs
items.text:
• Duplicate alert: the sheet shows an alert when a product code already exists.
  • Related sizes: the different sizes of the same product are linked together as related products, so they appear together, and the user chooses the size from the same product page.

items.title: Example
items.text:
A moisturizer is available in 40 ml and 90 ml.

  • Today: the two sizes appear as two separate products in different places on the website.
  • What the team needs: one product page shows the moisturizer, and the user chooses 40 ml or 90 ml from it.

items.title: Catalog and Admin Panel Problems
items.text: The catalog team reported these problems while auditing products. Most of them are in the admin panel (Backend and Frontend work), and some are related to the Audit Agent and Description Enhancement (AI work).

items.title: 1. Shades and Sizes
items.text:
• No shade field: a lipstick has shades such as "Nude 01" and "Red 05". There is no dedicated shade field in the admin panel, so shades are written inside the description. As a result, users cannot filter products by shade.
  • Shades are duplicated after editing: when the team changes "Nude 01" to "Nude 02", both shades appear together on the website.
  • Size is not visible in the admin panel: the size appears to users on the website, but the team cannot see or edit it in the admin panel.
  • Size breaks the product: adding a size changes the product status from "Successful" to "Failed". Writing the size in the title (such as "Cream 50 ml") causes an error, because the system needs a separate size field, and this field does not exist.

items.title: 2. Titles
items.text:
• Unclear titles: some titles say only "Cream", without the brand or the product type.
  • Bad formatting: titles are not bold and have no space under them, so they look merged with the description.
  • Arabic changes to English: any Arabic word written in the title is changed to English automatically.

items.title: 3. Descriptions (only 65% pass the audit)
items.text:
• No standard structure: each description should have 5 sections: Key Benefits, Ingredients/Materials, How to Use, Specifications, and Best Suited For. Most descriptions do not follow this structure.
  • Missing information: ingredients and usage steps are often missing. When the supplier does not send them, the Audit Agent marks the product as failed.
  • Perfume notes are missing: perfume listings do not include the top, middle, and base notes.
  • 5 required fields are missing: cruelty-free, vegan, made in, country of origin, and shelf life. These are the main reason why 35% of products fail the audit, and they also stop products from appearing in filters.

items.title: 4. Admin Panel Workflow
items.text:
• No bulk selection: the team cannot select many products and update them at once.
  • One product at a time: each product must be opened, edited, and confirmed alone, which takes a very long time.
  • No default values: when the supplier does not send a required field, such as country of manufacture, the system fails the product instead of filling a default value such as "Not Specified" or "Imported".

items.title: 5. Suggested Fixes
items.text:
• New fields: add Shade and Size fields in the admin panel.
  • Title formatting: make titles bold, with space under them.
  • Standard template: apply the 5-section structure to all descriptions.
  • Default values: fill missing fields automatically, so products can pass the audit.
  • Correct categories: classify products correctly, such as makeup brushes under beauty tools.

items.title: Admin Dashboard
items.text: Priority: Medium

items.title: The problem
items.text: Any change in the agent, such as changing information or following its performance, needs a developer. The team does not have one place to see how the agent is working.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
• Web-based configuration UI: the team changes the agent's settings without code.
  • Real-time monitoring and analytics: the team sees conversations and numbers as they happen.
  • Knowledge base management interface: the team adds or edits the information the agent answers from, such as the shipping and return policy.
  • User management and moderation: the team follows conversations and handles abuse.
  • Tool performance metrics.
  • System health dashboard: whether the agent is working or down.

items.title: Example
items.text: The shipping price to Jeddah changed. Instead of a developer changing the code, a team member opens the dashboard, edits the information in the knowledge base, and the agent answers with the new price right away.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Configuration: the team can change the agent's settings from the web.
  • FR-02: Monitoring: the dashboard shows conversations and numbers in real time.
  • FR-03: Knowledge base: the team can add, edit, and delete knowledge base information.
  • FR-04: User management: the team can view conversations and handle abusive ones.
  • FR-05: Tool performance: the dashboard shows tool speed and failure rate.
  • FR-06: System health: the dashboard shows the status of the agent and its parts.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Permissions: each team member can only see and edit what they are allowed to.
  • Ease of use: the dashboard is easy for the marketing and content team, not only for developers.
  • Change log: every change is recorded: who made it and when.

items.title: 3. Data Requirements
items.text:
• Current knowledge base information: all the information the agent currently answers from (shipping, returns, payment, FAQs), so it can be moved to the dashboard and edited easily.
  • List of editable settings: exactly what the team is allowed to change without a developer, such as the welcome message or shipping prices.
  • Performance numbers: response time, error rate, and tool usage, which come from Performance Metrics.
  • Conversation logs: for monitoring and user management, which depend on Conversation Memory Management.
  • Team roles and permissions: who in the team will use the dashboard, and what each person is allowed to do.

items.title: 4. Assessment
items.text:
In my view, this feature is useful, but it is better to build it inside GoCare's existing Admin Dashboard:

  • GoCare already has an Admin Dashboard, and it was decided in the meeting that the Analytics Dashboard will be inside it. So it is better to add agent pages inside it, instead of building a new dashboard.
  • The most important part is knowledge base management, because it lets the team update the agent's information without a developer.
  • The other parts (monitoring and tool performance) depend on Performance Metrics being built first.

items.title: Advanced Product Recommendations
items.text: Priority: Medium

items.title: The problem
items.text: When the user asks the agent for a recommendation, the agent searches products in a simple way. It does not use the recommendation system, so its suggestions are not based on the user's behavior or on what similar users bought.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature lets the agent show smarter recommendations inside the chat, by using the recommendation system:

  • Collaborative filtering based on user behavior: "Users like you also bought this."
  • Purchase history-based recommendations: products based on what the user bought before.
  • Context-aware product suggestions: products based on the situation, such as the time or the weather.
  • Similar product recommendations: products similar to the one the user is looking at.
  • Frequently bought together suggestions: products that are often bought together, such as a cleanser and a moisturizer.

items.title: Example
items.text:
User: Recommend something for me.

Agent: Customers who bought the same cleanser as you also liked this moisturizer. Would you like to see it? 😊

User: I'm buying this cleanser.

Agent: Customers often buy it together with this toner. Would you like to add it to your cart?

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Collaborative filtering: the agent shows products based on what similar users bought.
  • FR-02: Purchase history recommendations: the agent suggests products based on the user's past purchases.
  • FR-03: Context-aware suggestions: the agent adjusts suggestions to the user's situation.
  • FR-04: Similar products: the agent suggests products similar to the one the user is viewing.
  • FR-05: Frequently bought together: the agent suggests products that are often bought together.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Performance: recommendations must load quickly inside the chat.
  • Relevance: recommendations must match what the user is asking for.
  • Fallback: if the recommendation system is not available, the agent uses normal product search.
  • Consistency: recommendations in the chat must match the recommendations on the website.

items.title: 3. Assessment
items.text:
In my view, this feature is useful, but most of its work is in the recommendation system, not in the agent:

  • The agent only shows the results: the agent asks the recommendation system for suggestions, then shows them in the chat.
  • It overlaps with the recommendation roadmap: Collaborative Filtering and Context-Aware Recommendations are already planned in the recommendation system, and Context-Aware Recommendations was considered not important at the moment.

So the agent part is to connect the chat to the recommendation system once its features are ready.

items.title: Advanced Tool Management
items.text: Priority: Low

items.title: The problem
items.text: The agent uses tools, such as product search and the cart. As the number of tools grows, the agent may choose the wrong tool, the team does not know which tool fails, and adding a new tool needs code changes.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
• Dynamic tool loading and unloading: the agent loads only the tools it needs for the current request.
  • Tool usage optimization: reduces unnecessary tool calls.
  • Tool fallback strategies: uses another option when a tool fails.
  • Tool performance monitoring: the team knows which tool is slow or fails.
  • Custom tool creation interface: the team can add a tool without much code.

items.title: Example
items.text: The product search tool fails. Instead of saying "An error occurred", the agent uses a simpler search tool, and the user gets a normal answer.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Dynamic loading: the agent loads only the tools related to the request.
  • FR-02: Usage optimization: the agent does not call the same tool more than once without need.
  • FR-03: Fallback: each important tool has a fallback if it fails.
  • FR-04: Monitoring: the system records the speed and failure rate of each tool.
  • FR-05: Tool interface: the team can add or edit a tool from a simple interface.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Reliability: one failing tool must not stop the agent.
  • Security: new tools must be reviewed before they are used.
  • Performance: loading tools must not slow down the response.

items.title: 3. Data Requirements
items.text:
• Tool descriptions: the name of each tool, what it does, what inputs it needs, what it returns, and which request type it belongs to. The agent needs these descriptions to choose the right tool and load only what it needs.
  • Tool usage log: for every tool call: the tool name, the time, how long it took, whether it succeeded or failed, and which conversation it was in. Without it, we cannot know which tools are used the most, or which tools are slow.
  • Tool error log: the error type (timeout, API down, or wrong data), and how many times it happened. This shows which tools need a fallback the most.
  • Fallback list: for each important tool, what the fallback is if it fails. For example, if advanced search fails, use normal search. If there is no fallback, what exactly the agent tells the user.
  • Review rules for new tools: who reviews a new tool before it goes live, and what must be tested, so a tool with a problem does not reach users.

items.title: 4. Assessment
items.text:
In my view, this feature is not important at the moment:

  • The number of tools is still small, so loading them dynamically will not make a difference.
  • Fallback when a tool fails is already covered in Clarification & Fallback Handling.
  • Tool monitoring is already covered in Performance Metrics.
  • The tool interface needs high effort and has little value now.

items.title: Business Intelligence
items.text: Priority: Medium

items.title: The problem
items.text: Users' conversations with the agent contain important business information, such as the products users are looking for, but nobody uses this information.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature extracts business information from the conversations:

  • Product inquiry trends: which products users ask about the most.
  • Popular search terms: the words users use the most.
  • Category interest analysis: which categories users are interested in, such as skin care, hair care, or perfumes.
  • Peak usage times: when users use the chat the most.
  • User retention metrics: how many users come back to use the agent again.

items.title: Example
items.text: The marketing team finds that many users ask about a "serum for dark spots", and this product is not available on the website. So they decide to add it.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Product inquiries: the system shows the products users ask about the most.
  • FR-02: Search terms: the system shows the words users use the most.
  • FR-03: Categories: the system shows users' interest in each category.
  • FR-04: Peak times: the system shows the busiest usage times.
  • FR-05: Retention: the system shows the percentage of users who come back.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Privacy: reports show general numbers, not data about specific users.
  • Updates: reports are updated regularly, for example every week.
  • Readability: reports are clear for the marketing team, not only for developers.

items.title: 3. Data Requirements
items.text: Data Purpose Status Conversation Logs Find what users ask about Depends on Conversation Memory Management Products Mentioned in Conversations Find the most requested products Not collected yet Product Categories Analyze interest in each category Available on the website Message Timestamps Find peak usage times Available User IDs Measure how many users come back Depends on User Profiles & Authentication

items.title: 4. Assessment
items.text: In my view, this feature is important, because it shows the team what users ask about the most. This helps the marketing team know which products are in demand, and which products are missing from the website and need to be added.

items.title: Clarification & Fallback Handling
items.text: Priority: Medium

items.title: The problem
items.text: Users often send messages that are unclear, incomplete, or outside what the agent can do. When this happens, the agent may guess the wrong meaning, return an error, or give a confusing answer. This makes users lose trust in the assistant.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature helps the agent handle unclear or failed situations in a helpful way:

  • Ambiguous query clarification: asks the user what they mean when a message has more than one possible meaning.
  • Missing information requests: asks for the details needed to complete a request.
  • Graceful error recovery: handles technical errors, such as a failed tool call, without breaking the conversation.
  • "I don't understand" fallback responses: responds politely when it cannot understand the message.
  • Suggested alternative queries: suggests what the user could ask instead.

items.title: Example
items.text:
User: I want a cream.

Agent: Sure! Is it for your face, hands, or body? And what is your skin type?

(the product search tool fails)

Agent: Sorry, I couldn't load products right now. You can try again in a moment, or tell me the brand you're looking for and I'll help another way.

User: asdfgh

Agent: I didn't quite understand that. You can ask me things like "Show me sunscreens under 100 SAR" or "Track my order".

items.title: 2. Why It Matters
items.text:
• Fewer wrong answers: the agent asks instead of guessing.
  • No dead ends: users always know what to do next.
  • More trust: errors are handled calmly and clearly.
  • Better completion rate: more conversations end with the user getting what they need.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Ambiguous query clarification: the agent detects unclear requests and asks a short clarifying question.
  • FR-02: Missing information requests: the agent asks for missing details needed to complete a task, such as size, skin type, or address.
  • FR-03: Graceful error recovery: when a tool or service fails, the agent explains the problem simply and offers another option.
  • FR-04: Fallback responses: when the agent cannot understand a message, it responds politely instead of guessing.
  • FR-05: Suggested alternative queries: the agent suggests example questions the user can ask.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Balance: the agent should not ask too many questions; it should only clarify when really needed.
  • Consistency: fallback messages follow GoCare's tone in Arabic and English.
  • Reliability: errors are logged for the team to review.
  • Safety: technical error details are never shown to users.

items.title: 4. Risks
items.text:
• Too many questions: asking for clarification too often annoys users.
  • Hidden errors: friendly messages may hide real problems if errors are not logged.
  • Repetitive fallbacks: the same fallback message every time feels robotic.

items.title: In Scope
items.text:
• Clarifying questions for clearly ambiguous requests.
  • Requests for missing information in key actions, such as adding to cart.
  • Friendly error messages when tools fail.
  • Fallback responses with example questions.

items.title: Out of Scope (for now)
items.text:
• Smart, personalized alternative suggestions.
  • Analytics dashboards for fallback cases.

items.title: 6. Open Questions
items.text:
• When should the agent ask for clarification, and when should it make a reasonable assumption?
  • After how many failed attempts should the agent offer human support?
  • Is there a human support channel the agent can hand over to?

items.title: 7. Assessment
items.text: This feature is important, but there is an alternative: users already confirm their orders through WhatsApp. So even if the agent misunderstands a request, the order is checked with the user before it is completed.

items.title: Content Management
items.text: Priority: Low

items.title: The problem
items.text: The information the agent answers from, such as FAQs and offers, is fixed inside the code. So when there is a new offer or a season such as Ramadan or the Saudi National Day, the agent does not know about it until a developer changes the code. This means the agent may give old information, such as an offer that already ended, or miss new offers that could increase sales.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature lets the team manage the agent's content without a developer:

  • Dynamic FAQ management: the team adds, edits, and deletes FAQs and their answers.
  • Promotional content delivery: the agent knows the current offers and tells users about them when relevant.
  • Seasonal content updates: the agent talks about seasons, such as Ramadan offers or White Friday.
  • Banner and announcement system: short messages appear in the chat, such as "20% off today only".

items.title: Example
items.text:
Ramadan offers start. The marketing team adds the offer to the system, with a start date and an end date.

User: Are there any offers?

Agent: Yes! 25% off all skincare products during Ramadan. 🌙 The offer ends on the last day of Ramadan.

When Ramadan ends, the offer disappears automatically, and the agent stops mentioning it.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: FAQ management: the team can add, edit, and delete FAQs in Arabic and English.
  • FR-02: Promotional content: the agent knows the current offers and mentions them when the user asks or when they are related to the products she is looking at.
  • FR-03: Seasonal content: the team can add seasonal content with a start and end date.
  • FR-04: Announcements: the team can add a short announcement that appears in the chat for a set period.
  • FR-05: Content preview: the team can preview how the agent will answer with the new content before publishing it.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Ease of use: the marketing team can edit content without a developer.
  • Fast updates: changes appear in the agent's answers right away.
  • Automatic expiry: offers and seasonal content disappear automatically when their end date passes.
  • Approval: content is reviewed before it is shown to users.
  • Language support: all content is available in Arabic and English.

items.title: 3. Data Requirements
items.text:
• Current FAQs: all the FAQs on the website and their answers, in Arabic and English, as the starting point.
  • Current offers: for each offer: its name, details, the products or categories it covers, the discount value, and its start and end dates.
  • Seasons calendar: the important seasons for Saudi customers (Ramadan, Eid, Saudi National Day, White Friday), their dates, and the suitable content for each one.
  • Announcement content: the text of each announcement, where and when it appears, and its end date.
  • Content approval process: who in the team reviews content before it is shown to users, and how long the review takes.

items.title: 4. Assessment
items.text:
In my view, this feature is not important as a separate feature:

  • FAQ management is already covered in the Admin Dashboard (knowledge base management).
  • Promotional content overlaps with Personalized Marketing, which the marketing team reviews.
  • The better option is to add it as part of the Admin Dashboard, instead of building it as a separate feature.

items.title: Context Awareness
items.text: Priority: High · Effort: High

items.title: The problem
items.text: People do not talk in complete, separate sentences. They refer to things mentioned earlier, ask short follow-up questions, and change topics. Without context awareness, the agent cannot understand messages such as "the second one", "is it suitable for me?", or "add it to the cart".

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature helps the agent understand a conversation as a whole:

  • Understands conversations across multiple turns.
  • Resolves references, such as "it", "this one", "the second one", and "that product".
  • Handles follow-up questions.
  • Tracks the current topic, and handles topic changes.
  • Keeps track of the conversation state (e.g. browsing, comparing, adding to cart, checkout).

items.title: Example
items.text:
User: Show me vitamin C serums.

Agent: (shows three products)

User: How much is the second one?

User: Is it suitable for oily skin?

User: Has my last order shipped yet?

User: OK, add the serum to my cart.

The agent must know that "the second one", "it", and "the serum" all refer to the same product, and that the question about the order was a temporary topic change.

items.title: 2. Why It Matters
items.text:
• Natural conversations: users can talk normally, without repeating product names.
  • Fewer mistakes: the agent acts on the right product.
  • Better shopping flow: browsing, comparing, and adding to cart happen smoothly in one conversation.
  • Required for complex features: such as building a skincare routine in the chat.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Multi-turn understanding: the agent understands each message in the context of previous messages.
  • FR-02: Reference resolution: the agent links references (pronouns, "that product", "the second one") to the correct item.
  • FR-03: Follow-up question handling: the agent answers short follow-up questions about the current item or topic.
  • FR-04: Topic tracking and switching: the agent detects topic changes, and can return to the previous topic.
  • FR-05: Conversation state management: the agent tracks the current stage of the conversation, such as browsing, comparing, cart, or checkout.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Accuracy: references must be resolved correctly, especially before actions such as adding to cart.
  • Safety: when a reference is unclear, the agent must ask for clarification instead of guessing.
  • Performance: context handling must not noticeably slow down responses.
  • Language support: works in Arabic and English, including mixed messages.

items.title: 4. Technical Approach
items.text:
• Structured state in LangGraph: besides the message history, store structured context in the graph state, such as last_shown_products, current_product, current_topic, and conversation_stage.
  • Reference resolution: when the agent shows products, save them in order in the state. References like "the second one" are mapped to that list.
  • Query rewriting: before calling tools, the agent rewrites short follow-up messages into complete requests (e.g. "is it suitable for oily skin?" becomes "is Vitamin C Serum X suitable for oily skin?").
  • Topic tracking: save the current topic in the state, and keep the previous topic when the user temporarily switches.
  • Clarification: if a reference matches more than one item, the agent asks the user which one they mean.

items.title: Dependencies
items.text:
• Conversation Memory Management, to keep the conversation history and state.
  • Session Management, to keep the state tied to the right conversation.
  • Marketplace and cart tools that return product IDs, so references can be linked to real products.

items.title: Risks
items.text:
• Wrong references: the agent may add the wrong product to the cart.
  • Ambiguity: messages like "this one" may be unclear when several products were discussed.
  • Arabic references: Arabic pronouns and dialect expressions (e.g. "ده", "اللي قبله") make resolution harder.
  • Higher costs: query rewriting adds extra model calls.

items.title: In Scope
items.text:
• Multi-turn understanding using the conversation history.
  • Resolving references to recently shown products, such as "the second one" and "it".
  • Follow-up question handling for the current product.
  • Clarification when a reference is unclear.

items.title: Out of Scope (for now)
items.text:
• Advanced topic switching and returning to older topics.
  • Full conversation stage management across all flows.
  • Resolving references across different sessions.

items.title: 7. Open Questions
items.text: • Should context be kept when the user returns to a session later?

items.title: 8. Business Impact
items.text:
• Faster buying: the user can say "add the second one to the cart" without typing the product name.
  • Fewer order mistakes: the agent adds the right product, so returns and complaints go down.

items.title: Example
items.text: A user sees three serums and says "How much is the second one? Add it to my cart." The agent understands directly, and the purchase is done in seconds.

items.title: Conversation Analytics
items.text: Priority: Medium

items.title: The problem
items.text: The team does not know what users talk about with the agent, where they leave the conversation, or how many conversations end with a purchase. So it is hard to know what the agent needs to improve.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature analyzes users' conversations with the agent:

  • Intent classification and tracking: what users ask about the most, such as products, orders, or shipping.
  • Sentiment analysis: whether users are happy or unhappy in the conversation.
  • Common query patterns: the most frequent questions.
  • Drop-off points identification: where users leave the conversation.
  • User satisfaction metrics: measures of how satisfied users are with the conversations.
  • Conversion funnel analysis: how many conversations start with a question and end with a purchase.

items.title: Example
items.text:
The team opens the report and finds:

  • 40% of the questions are about sunscreen.
  • Many users leave the conversation after asking about the shipping price.
  • 15% of conversations end with a purchase.

So the team understands that the shipping answer needs to be improved.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Intent classification: the system classifies each conversation by request type.
  • FR-02: Sentiment analysis: the system detects whether a conversation is positive or negative.
  • FR-03: Common queries: the system shows the most frequent questions.
  • FR-04: Drop-off points: the system detects the stage where users leave the conversation.
  • FR-05: Satisfaction metrics: the system shows user satisfaction measures.
  • FR-06: Conversion funnel: the system shows how many conversations reach each stage until purchase.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Privacy: the analysis does not show users' personal data.
  • Performance: the analysis does not affect the agent's response speed.
  • Accuracy: classification must be accurate in Arabic and English.

items.title: 3. Data Requirements
items.text: Data Purpose Status Conversation Logs Analyze what users talk about Depends on Conversation Memory Management Message Intent Labels Know the type of each request Not available; can come from the existing message classification guardrail Conversation End Point Find where users leave the conversation Not collected yet Order Data Linked to Conversations Know if a conversation ended with a purchase Not available User Feedback Ratings Measure user satisfaction Depends on Feedback Collection

items.title: 4. Assessment
items.text:
In my view, this feature is useful, but it is not a high priority at the moment:

  • Sentiment analysis was considered not needed now in the meeting, and its source is the website comments.
  • The results need the Analytics Dashboard to be shown, which is not a top priority.
  • The effort is high.

items.title: Conversation Flow Control
items.text: Priority: Medium

items.title: The problem
items.text: Users come to the agent for many different reasons: searching for products, asking questions, managing their cart, or getting help with an order. Some tasks also need several steps, such as building a skincare routine or checking out. Without clear flow control, the agent may handle every message the same way, lose track of multi-step tasks, or get confused when the user interrupts or changes the subject.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature controls how conversations move between tasks and steps:

  • Intent classification and routing: understands what the user wants and sends the request to the right part of the agent.
  • Conversation branching: follows different paths depending on the user's answers.
  • Step-by-step guided workflows: guides users through multi-step tasks, one step at a time.
  • Conversation interruption handling: handles questions in the middle of a task, then returns to the task.
  • Topic switching detection: detects when the user moves to a completely new topic.

items.title: Example
items.text:
User: I want to build a skincare routine.

Agent: Great! Step 1 of 3: What is your skin type?

User: Oily. Wait, how much is shipping to Jeddah?

Agent: Shipping to Jeddah is 25 SAR. Now, back to your routine: Step 2 of 3: What is your main concern?

The agent recognized the routine-building intent, started a guided workflow, answered the interruption, then continued the workflow.

items.title: 2. Why It Matters
items.text:
• Right answer for each request: each type of request is handled by the right logic and tools.
  • Complex tasks become easy: step-by-step guidance helps users complete multi-step tasks.
  • No lost progress: interruptions do not reset the task.
  • Easier to extend: new tasks can be added as new routes or workflows.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Intent classification and routing: the agent classifies each message (e.g. product search, product question, cart, order, knowledge base, out of scope) and routes it to the right handler.
  • FR-02: Conversation branching: the agent follows different paths based on the user's answers.
  • FR-03: Guided workflows: the agent supports multi-step workflows, showing the current step and remembering previous answers.
  • FR-04: Interruption handling: the agent answers interruptions and then returns to the current workflow.
  • FR-05: Topic switching detection: the agent detects a real topic change and asks whether to continue or cancel the current task.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Accuracy: intent classification must be accurate, with a safe default when unsure.
  • Performance: routing must not noticeably slow down responses.
  • Maintainability: workflows must be easy to add and change.
  • Language support: works in Arabic and English.

items.title: 4. Technical Approach
items.text:
• Router node in LangGraph: a node at the start of the graph classifies the intent and routes to the right sub-graph or set of tools.
  • Reuse the existing guardrail: the current message classification guardrail already separates in-scope and out-of-scope messages. Intent classification can extend it with more detailed categories.
  • Workflows as sub-graphs: each guided workflow (e.g. skincare routine, checkout) is a LangGraph sub-graph with its own steps and state.
  • Workflow state: save the active workflow, current step, and collected answers in the conversation state.
  • Interruptions: if a message does not belong to the current step, handle it as a side question, then return to the saved step.
  • Topic switching: if the user clearly starts a new task, ask whether to pause or cancel the current one.

items.title: Conversation Memory Management
items.text: Priority: High · Effort: High

items.title: The problem
items.text: The GoCare agent is currently stateless: each message is handled as if it were the first one. The language model itself does not remember anything between messages, so the agent cannot recall what the user said earlier in the conversation, or in previous conversations.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature gives the agent memory at two levels:

  • Short-term memory: remembers what was said in the current conversation.
  • Long-term memory: remembers important information about the user across conversations, such as skin type, preferred brands, or allergies.

It also stores conversation history permanently, keeps each user's memory separate, and summarizes long conversations so they stay fast and affordable.

items.title: Example
items.text:
User: My skin is oily.

(three messages later)

User: Can you recommend a moisturizer?

Agent: Since your skin is oily, here is a light gel moisturizer...

(the same user returns a week later)

Agent: Welcome back! Last time you were looking for products for oily skin. Would you like to continue?

items.title: 2. Why It Matters
items.text:
• Users do not repeat themselves: the agent remembers what they already said.
  • More personal recommendations: answers use the user's known preferences.
  • Foundation for other features: Context Awareness and the Skincare Routine Advisor both depend on memory.
  • Continuity: users can return to previous conversations without losing anything.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Short-term memory: the agent keeps the context of the current session and uses it in every response.
  • FR-02: Long-term memory: the agent stores and reuses important user preferences and history across sessions.
  • FR-03: Conversation history persistence: conversations are stored permanently and are not lost after a restart or a closed page.
  • FR-04: Context retention across messages: the agent connects related messages into one request (e.g. "shampoo", "for colored hair", "under 100 SAR").
  • FR-05: User-specific memory isolation: each user's memory is accessible only to that user.
  • FR-06: Memory summarization: older parts of long conversations are summarized, while recent messages are kept in full.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Privacy & Security: memory must never leak between users, and must follow data protection regulations in Saudi Arabia.
  • Performance: loading memory must not noticeably slow down responses.
  • Cost: summarization must keep the number of tokens sent to the model under control.
  • Scalability: memory must work across multiple agent instances, in line with the current stateless, horizontally scalable design.
  • Reliability: if the memory store is unavailable, the agent must still answer, without memory.

items.title: 4. Technical Approach
items.text:
• Short-term memory and persistence: use a LangGraph checkpointer to save the conversation state after each step, backed by a shared database such as PostgreSQL or Redis, so any agent instance can continue the conversation.
  • Thread per conversation: each conversation has a unique thread_id, linked to the user's ID.
  • Long-term memory: use a LangGraph store (or a dedicated table) to save extracted facts per user, such as skin type, hair type, preferred brands, and allergies.
  • Memory extraction: after each conversation, or at key moments, the agent extracts important facts and saves them to long-term memory.
  • Summarization: when a conversation exceeds a set length, older messages are replaced with a short summary, and only the last N messages are kept in full.
  • Isolation: every read and write is filtered by the authenticated user ID, never by an ID sent in the message.

items.title: Dependencies
items.text:
• Session Management, to identify conversations and users.
  • A shared database for memory and checkpoints.
  • A stable user ID from authentication.

items.title: Risks
items.text:
• Memory leakage between users: a bug could show one user's information to another. This is the most serious risk.
  • Wrong long-term facts: the agent may save something incorrect, such as the wrong skin type, and keep using it.
  • Lost details in summaries: important information may be dropped when summarizing.
  • Higher costs: sending more context with each message increases model usage.

items.title: In Scope
items.text:
• Short-term memory within a conversation.
  • Conversation history persistence using a LangGraph checkpointer.
  • User-specific memory isolation.

items.title: Out of Scope (for now)
items.text:
• Long-term memory across conversations.
  • Automatic memory summarization.
  • A screen for users to view or delete their memory.

items.title: 7. Open Questions
items.text:
• Which database should be used: PostgreSQL, Redis, or the existing database?
  • How long should conversations and long-term memory be kept?
  • Should guest users (not logged in) have memory?

items.title: 8. Business Impact
items.text:
• Higher conversion: the agent remembers what the user is looking for, so it reaches the right product faster, and the user is more likely to buy.
  • Fewer abandoned conversations: users leave less often when they do not have to repeat their skin type, budget, or preferences.
  • More returning customers: when the agent welcomes the user back and continues from where they stopped, the user is more likely to return and buy again.
  • Better personal recommendations: recommendations based on what the user already said lead to more relevant products and larger orders.
  • Controlled model costs: summarizing long conversations keeps the number of tokens low, so costs do not grow with conversation length.

items.title: Example
items.text: A user tells the agent that her skin is oily and her budget is under 100 SAR. Without memory, she has to repeat this in every message, and she may leave. With memory, the agent recommends suitable products directly, and she buys in the same conversation.

items.title: Customer Profile Integration
items.text: Priority: Low

items.title: The problem
items.text: The agent does not know anything about the user's account on GoCare. It cannot see what she bought before, her saved addresses, or her wishlist, so she has to repeat this information, and the agent cannot use it to help her.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature connects the agent to the user's GoCare account:

  • Purchase history access: the agent knows what the user bought before.
  • Saved addresses and payment methods: the agent uses the user's saved details, so she does not type them again.
  • Order preferences and recurring orders: the agent knows products the user orders regularly.
  • Wishlist management: the user can add or remove products from her wishlist through the chat.
  • Recent views and interactions: the agent knows the products the user viewed recently.

items.title: Example
items.text:
User: Add this serum to my wishlist.

Agent: Done! The serum is now in your wishlist. ❤️

User: Recommend something for me.

Agent: You bought a vitamin C serum last month. This sunscreen goes well with it. Would you like to see it?

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Purchase history access: the agent can read the user's past purchases.
  • FR-02: Saved addresses and payment methods: the agent can use the user's saved addresses and payment methods.
  • FR-03: Order preferences and recurring orders: the agent knows the user's regular orders and preferences.
  • FR-04: Wishlist management: the agent can show, add, and remove wishlist products.
  • FR-05: Recent views and interactions: the agent can use the products the user viewed recently.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Security: the agent can only access the data of the logged-in user.
  • Privacy: payment details must never be shown in full in the chat.
  • Accuracy: profile data must match the user's account on the website.
  • Performance: loading profile data must not slow down responses.

items.title: 3. Assessment
items.text:
In my view, this feature is not a high priority at the moment, because it overlaps with other features:

  • User Profiles & Authentication: both features are about knowing the user and her data.
  • User Preferences & Settings: both features save the user's preferences.
  • Personalization Engine: both features use the user's past purchases to suggest products.

The most useful part of this feature is using past purchases in recommendations, and this is already covered by the Personalization Engine.

items.title: Feedback Collection
items.text: Priority: High

items.title: The problem
items.text: The team cannot easily know whether users are happy with the agent's answers. Without feedback, it is hard to find wrong answers, understand what users need, or measure whether changes improve the agent.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature collects feedback from users about the agent:

  • Message-level feedback: thumbs up or thumbs down on each answer.
  • Conversation rating system: a rating for the whole conversation, such as 1 to 5 stars.
  • Detailed feedback forms: a short form to explain what went wrong or what could be better.
  • Issue reporting mechanism: a way to report a problem, such as a wrong price or broken link.
  • Feature request collection: a way for users to suggest new features.

items.title: Example
items.text:
Agent: Here are 3 sunscreens for oily skin... 👍 👎

(the user taps 👎)

Agent: Sorry about that! What was wrong? [ Wrong products ] [ Too long ] [ Wrong price ] [ Other ]

(at the end of the conversation)

Agent: How was your experience today? ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

items.title: 2. Why It Matters
items.text:
• Find wrong answers quickly: negative feedback shows exactly which answers need fixing.
  • Measure quality: feedback scores show whether the agent is improving over time.
  • Understand users: issue reports and feature requests show what users really need.
  • Low effort, high value: simple to build, and useful for every other feature.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Message-level feedback: users can rate each answer with thumbs up or down.
  • FR-02: Conversation rating: users can rate the whole conversation.
  • FR-03: Detailed feedback forms: users can explain their feedback with a short form or predefined reasons.
  • FR-04: Issue reporting: users can report specific problems with an answer.
  • FR-05: Feature request collection: users can suggest new features.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Non-intrusive: feedback requests must not interrupt or annoy users.
  • Traceability: each feedback item is linked to the exact message, conversation, and user.
  • Privacy: feedback is stored securely, in line with data protection regulations in Saudi Arabia.
  • Reporting: the team can view and analyze feedback easily.

items.title: 4. Technical Approach
items.text:
• Feedback API: an endpoint that saves feedback with message_id, conversation_id, user_id, rating, reason, and comment.
  • Message IDs: each agent answer gets a unique ID, so feedback can be linked to it.
  • Frontend buttons: thumbs up and down under each answer, and a rating at the end of the conversation.
  • Predefined reasons: simple reason buttons for negative feedback, plus an optional comment.
  • Storage and review: save feedback in a database table, and show summaries in the Analytics Dashboard.
  • Tracing: link feedback to conversation logs, so the team can see the full context of a bad answer.

items.title: Dependencies
items.text:
• Frontend support for feedback buttons and forms.
  • Session Management and Conversation Memory Management, to link feedback to conversations.
  • A place to review feedback, such as the Analytics Dashboard.

items.title: Risks
items.text:
• Low response rate: many users do not leave feedback.
  • Biased feedback: unhappy users are more likely to give feedback than happy ones.
  • No follow-up: collecting feedback has no value if nobody reviews it.

items.title: 6. Open Questions
items.text:
• Who will review feedback, and how often?
  • Should the conversation rating appear at the end of every conversation, or only sometimes?
  • Should feedback be shown in the Analytics Dashboard?

items.title: Interactive Elements
items.text: Priority: Medium

items.title: The problem
items.text: Today, users interact with the agent mainly by typing. Typing every request takes effort, especially on mobile, and showing products as plain text is less attractive than showing them with images and buttons.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature adds interactive elements to the chat:

  • Quick reply suggestions: small buttons with suggested answers, such as "Oily skin" or "Dry skin".
  • Button-based actions: buttons for actions, such as "Add to cart" or "View details".
  • Carousel for product display: products shown as cards with image, name, and price, which the user can swipe through.
  • Suggested follow-up questions: buttons with possible next questions after each answer.
  • Form-based data collection: small forms inside the chat for collecting several details at once, such as an address.

items.title: Example
items.text:
Agent: What is your skin type?

[ Oily ] [ Dry ] [ Combination ] [ Sensitive ]

Agent: Here are some moisturizers for oily skin:

(a carousel of product cards, each with an image, name, price, and an "Add to cart" button)

[ Compare these ] [ Show cheaper options ]

items.title: 2. Why It Matters
items.text:
• Faster interaction: users tap instead of typing.
  • Better on mobile: easier to use on small screens.
  • More attractive product display: images and prices increase interest.
  • Higher conversion: "Add to cart" buttons shorten the path to purchase.
  • Guided conversations: suggestions show users what the agent can do.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Quick reply suggestions: the agent can send suggested replies as buttons.
  • FR-02: Button-based actions: product messages include action buttons, such as "Add to cart" and "View details".
  • FR-03: Product carousel: the agent can show multiple products as swipeable cards.
  • FR-04: Suggested follow-up questions: the agent can suggest the next questions as buttons.
  • FR-05: Form-based data collection: the agent can show a small form to collect structured information.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Fallback to text: if an element cannot be displayed, the same information is shown as text.
  • Mobile-friendly: elements work well on small screens.
  • Accessibility and language: elements support Arabic and English, including right-to-left layout.
  • Consistency: the same element types are used across all features.

items.title: 4. Technical Approach
items.text:
• Structured response format: the agent returns structured data along with the text, such as quick_replies, buttons, carousel, and form, instead of only plain text.
  • Frontend components: the chat interface renders each element type (buttons, cards, forms).
  • Actions: when a user taps a button, the frontend sends a defined action (e.g. add_to_cart with a product ID) back to the agent.
  • Product cards: use product data from the marketplace tools, such as image, name, price, and ID.
  • Streaming: text can be streamed first, and interactive elements added at the end of the response.

items.title: Loyalty Program Integration
items.text: Priority: Low

items.title: The problem
items.text: GoCare has loyalty points for its customers, but when a user wants to know how many points she has, when they expire, or how to use them, she has to search the website. The agent does not know anything about her points, so it cannot remind her to use them or tell her about offers made only for loyalty members. As a result, many users forget their points, and the points expire without being used.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature connects the agent to GoCare's loyalty program:

  • Points balance queries: the user asks the agent how many points she has, and when they expire.
  • Rewards redemption: the user uses her points for a discount, free shipping, or a gift, directly from the chat.
  • Tier status information: the user knows her membership level (for example, Silver or Gold), its benefits, and how much she needs to reach the next level.
  • Special offers for loyalty members: the agent shows offers that are available only to loyalty members.

items.title: Example
items.text:
User: How many points do I have?

Agent: You have 450 points, which equals a 45 SAR discount on your next order. 120 of these points expire at the end of this month. Would you like to use them now? 🎁

User: How far am I from Gold?

Agent: You need 300 more points to reach Gold. Gold members get free shipping on every order.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Points balance: the agent shows the user's current points balance, their value in SAR, and the points that will expire soon.
  • FR-02: Rewards redemption: the agent shows the available rewards and helps the user use her points on her cart or next order.
  • FR-03: Tier status: the agent shows the user's current level, its benefits, and the points or orders needed for the next level.
  • FR-04: Special offers: the agent shows the offers available for the user's level.
  • FR-05: Expiry reminders: the agent reminds the user about points that will expire soon when she starts a conversation.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Accuracy: the points balance must match the website exactly, because a wrong number damages trust.
  • Confirmation: the agent must get a clear confirmation from the user before using her points.
  • Security: the user can only see and use her own points, and only when she is logged in.
  • Consistency: the rules shown by the agent must be the same as the rules on the website.
  • Language support: works in Arabic and English.

items.title: 3. Data Requirements
items.text:
• Loyalty program rules: how users earn points (for example, one point for each SAR), how many points equal one SAR, the minimum points needed for redemption, and when points expire.
  • User points balance: an API that returns the current points balance for each user, the points history, and the expiry date of each group of points.
  • Tiers and their conditions: the names of the levels, the points or number of orders needed for each level, and the benefits of each level, such as free shipping or extra discounts.
  • Available rewards: a list of what the user can redeem her points for (discount, free shipping, gift), how many points each reward needs, and any conditions, such as a minimum order value.
  • Current special offers: the active offers for loyalty members, which levels they are for, and their start and end dates.
  • Redemption API: an API that lets the agent apply points to the user's cart or order safely, and returns the result.

items.title: 4. Assessment
items.text:
In my view, this feature is not important at the moment:

  • The website already shows the points: the user can see her points from her account on the website.
  • It needs backend work first: the agent needs APIs for the points balance, rewards, and redemption before it can do anything.
  • Redemption is sensitive: using points affects the order price, so any mistake costs money and needs strong confirmation.
  • A simple first step: later, we can start with showing the points balance and expiry only, without redemption.

items.title: Multi-Agent Workflows
items.text: Priority: Low

items.title: The problem
items.text: Today, one agent does everything: it searches for products, answers skincare questions, and handles orders. As tasks grow, one agent may get confused, and its prompt becomes large and hard to change.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature divides the work between several agents, each one specialized in one area:

  • Supervisor agent: understands what the user wants and sends the request to the right agent.
  • Specialized agents: a product expert, a skincare specialist, and an order handler.
  • Agent collaboration and handoff: agents pass the conversation to each other.
  • Task delegation and coordination: a large task is divided between them.

items.title: Example
items.text:
User: I want a routine for my oily skin, and where is my last order?

  • The supervisor splits the request into two parts.
  • The skincare specialist builds the routine.
  • The order handler gets the order status.
  • The supervisor combines both answers and sends them to the user.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Supervisor agent: classifies each request and sends it to the right agent.
  • FR-02: Specialized agents: each agent has its own tools and instructions for its area.
  • FR-03: Handoff: an agent can pass the conversation to another agent without losing context.
  • FR-04: Task delegation: the supervisor can split a request into several tasks and combine the results.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Performance: having several agents must not slow down the response much.
  • Cost: the number of model calls must not increase without need.
  • Consistency: the user must feel she is talking to one assistant, not several.

items.title: 3. Data Requirements
items.text:
• Request categories: a clear list of request types users ask about (product search, skincare question, order, shipping, cart), with real message examples for each type in Arabic and English. The supervisor needs this to send each message to the right agent, and it can start from the categories in the existing message classification guardrail.
  • Tool assignment per agent: a list of all existing tools, and which agent owns each tool. For example, product search belongs to the product expert, and order status belongs to the order handler. We must make sure no important tool is left without an agent.
  • Instructions for each agent: a separate system prompt for each agent, with its area, what it is allowed to do, and when to return the request to the supervisor.
  • Shared conversation state: one place that all agents read from and write to: previous messages, products shown, and user information such as skin type. Without it, the user would have to repeat herself every time the request moves to another agent.
  • Handoff log: a record of every time the conversation moved from one agent to another, and why. The team needs it to check whether the supervisor routes requests correctly.

items.title: 4. Assessment
items.text:
In my view, this feature is not a priority at the moment:

  • The effort is very high.
  • It overlaps with Conversation Flow Control, which already includes a router that directs requests.
  • Higher cost, because each agent uses the model.
  • One agent with tools is enough until the number of tasks really grows.

items.title: Multi-Channel Support
items.text: Priority: Medium

items.title: The problem
items.text: The agent works only inside the website chat. But many customers in Saudi Arabia use WhatsApp and Instagram more than the website, so when they want to ask about a product, they have to open the website first.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature lets the same agent answer customers in more than one place:

  • WhatsApp: through the WhatsApp Business API.
  • Instagram: answering DM messages.
  • Facebook Messenger.
  • SMS messages.
  • Email.

It is the same agent, with the same knowledge, not a new chatbot.

items.title: Example
items.text: A user sees a GoCare ad on Instagram and sends a DM: "Is this serum suitable for sensitive skin?" The agent answers her in the same DM and sends her the product link.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: WhatsApp: the agent receives and answers WhatsApp messages.
  • FR-02: Instagram: the agent receives and answers Instagram DM messages.
  • FR-03: Facebook Messenger: the agent receives and answers Messenger messages.
  • FR-04: SMS: the agent can send and receive SMS messages.
  • FR-05: Email: the agent can answer emails.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Same experience: the agent answers with the same quality and style in every channel.
  • Message format: the answer is adapted to each channel, because, for example, WhatsApp does not support the same buttons and cards as the website.
  • Compliance: the agent follows each platform's rules, such as WhatsApp messaging rules.
  • Privacy: customer data is protected in all channels.

items.title: 3. Data Requirements
items.text:
• WhatsApp Business API account: an official, active account, a dedicated phone number, and message templates approved by Meta. This is the same account needed for Churn Prediction.
  • Social media account access: access to GoCare's Instagram and Facebook accounts, so the agent can read and answer messages.
  • Linking the user's identity across channels: a way to know that a WhatsApp number belongs to the same user who has an account on the website, usually through the phone number.
  • Message format rules for each channel: what is allowed in each channel (images, links, buttons, message length), so the answer is displayed correctly.
  • Conversation logs from all channels: all conversations are saved in one place, with the name of the channel they came from.

items.title: 4. Assessment
items.text:
In my view, only WhatsApp is important at the moment, and the other channels can wait:

  • Users already confirm their orders on WhatsApp, so this is where they are.
  • The WhatsApp Business API is already needed for Churn Prediction, so the same work serves both features.
  • Instagram, Facebook, SMS, and email need very high effort and have less value now.

items.title: Order Management
items.text: Priority: Low

items.title: The problem
items.text: Today, when a user wants to know where her order is, cancel it, or return a product, she has to search the website or contact customer service. The agent cannot help her with her orders.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature lets the user manage her orders directly from the chat:

  • Order status tracking: the user asks about the status of her order.
  • Order history retrieval: the user sees her past orders.
  • Cancellation and modification support: the user can cancel an order or change details, such as the address.
  • Return and refund assistance: the agent helps the user return a product and get her money back.
  • Delivery tracking: the user knows where her shipment is and when it will arrive.

items.title: Example
items.text:
User: Where is my order?

Agent: Your order #1234 was shipped yesterday, and it will arrive tomorrow. 🚚

User: The cream arrived damaged. What should I do?

Agent: Sorry about that! I can start a return request for you. Would you like a refund or a replacement?

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Order status tracking: the agent shows the current status of the user's order.
  • FR-02: Order history retrieval: the agent shows the user's past orders.
  • FR-03: Cancellation and modification: the agent can cancel an order or change its details, if the order has not been shipped yet.
  • FR-04: Return and refund assistance: the agent guides the user through the return process and starts a return request.
  • FR-05: Delivery tracking: the agent shows the shipment location and the expected delivery date.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Security: the user can only see and change her own orders.
  • Confirmation: the agent must ask the user to confirm before cancelling or changing an order.
  • Accuracy: order information must be up to date and match the website.
  • Performance: order information must load quickly.
  • Language support: works in Arabic and English.

items.title: 3. Assessment
items.text:
In my view, this feature is not a high priority at the moment, for these reasons:

  • Orders are already confirmed through WhatsApp: the user already talks with the team on WhatsApp about her order, so she can ask about its status there.
  • The website already shows order information: the user can see her order status and order history from her account on the website.
  • Cancellation and refunds are sensitive: letting the agent cancel orders or start refunds needs strong confirmation and backend support, and a mistake can cost money.
  • It needs backend work first: the agent needs order, shipping, and return APIs before it can answer any order question.

items.title: Performance Metrics
items.text: Priority: Medium

items.title: The problem
items.text: The team does not know if the agent is working well from a technical side: Is it fast? Does it make many errors? Which tools fail? So problems may stay without anyone noticing.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature measures the agent's performance:

  • Response time monitoring: how long the agent takes to answer.
  • Tool usage statistics: which tools are used the most.
  • Success rate tracking: how many requests the agent completes successfully.
  • Error rate monitoring: how many times the agent or its tools fail.
  • User engagement metrics: how much users use the agent.

items.title: Example
items.text: The team finds that the average response time became 8 seconds instead of 3 seconds, and that the product search tool fails 10% of the time. So they know where the problem is and fix it quickly.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Response time: the system measures the time of each response.
  • FR-02: Tool usage: the system records each tool used and how many times.
  • FR-03: Success rate: the system measures the percentage of requests completed successfully.
  • FR-04: Error rate: the system records errors and their types.
  • FR-05: User engagement: the system shows the number of conversations and messages.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Performance: measuring must not slow down the agent.
  • Alerts: the team receives an alert if errors or response time go above a set limit.
  • Reliability: metrics data is kept even if the agent restarts.

items.title: 3. Data Requirements
items.text: Data Purpose Status Response Time per Message Measure the agent's speed Not collected yet Tool Call Logs Know which tools are used and how often Not collected yet Error Logs Measure the error rate and its causes Partly available through the existing logs Request Outcome (success or failure) Measure the success rate Not collected yet Number of Conversations and Messages Measure user engagement Depends on Session Management

items.title: 4. Assessment
items.text:
In my view, this feature is important for the team:

  • It helps the team find problems quickly, before users get annoyed.
  • It is not hard, and part of it already exists in the health monitoring endpoints.
  • It has a small overlap with Session Management (number of sessions) and Feedback Collection (user satisfaction).

items.title: Personalization Engine
items.text: Priority: Medium · Effort: High

items.title: The problem
items.text: Even with memory and saved preferences, the agent still answers every user in the same general way. It does not adapt its greeting, its content, or its tone to who the user is, how they behave, or what time it is.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The Personalization Engine adapts the agent's responses to each user:

  • Personalized greetings and responses: greeting returning users by name, and referring to their recent activity.
  • Behavior-based content adaptation: adapting answers based on what the user usually browses or buys.
  • Time-of-day awareness: adapting suggestions to the time of day, such as morning or night routines.
  • User journey tracking: knowing where the user is in their shopping journey (e.g. new visitor, browsing, comparing, returning customer).
  • Adaptive response tone: adapting the tone and length of answers to the user's style.

items.title: Example
items.text:
Morning, returning user: Agent: Good morning, Sara! Your sunscreen from last month may be running low. Would you like to reorder it?

Night, new user: Agent: Welcome to GoCare! Are you looking for anything for your night routine?

items.title: 2. Why It Matters
items.text:
• Better engagement: personal conversations feel more natural and helpful.
  • Higher conversion: suggestions match the user's behavior and timing.
  • Repeat purchases: reminders based on past purchases encourage reordering.
  • Builds loyalty: users feel the assistant knows them.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Personalized greetings and responses: the agent greets users by name and refers to relevant past activity.
  • FR-02: Behavior-based content adaptation: the agent adapts suggestions to the user's browsing and purchase behavior.
  • FR-03: Time-of-day awareness: the agent adapts suggestions to the current time of day.
  • FR-04: User journey tracking: the agent identifies the user's current stage in their shopping journey.
  • FR-05: Adaptive response tone: the agent adapts its tone and answer length to the user's communication style.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Privacy: personalization must not feel intrusive, and must only use data the user agreed to share.
  • Transparency: users should understand why they see personalized suggestions.
  • Performance: personalization must not noticeably slow down responses.
  • Fallback: if personalization data is missing, the agent answers normally.

items.title: 4. Technical Approach
items.text:
• User context builder: at the start of each conversation, build a small user context from the profile, preferences, long-term memory, and recent orders.
  • Prompt personalization: add this context to the system prompt, such as the user's name, language, tone, and recent purchases.
  • Journey stage: a simple rule-based classifier based on account age, number of orders, and recent activity (e.g. "new", "browsing", "returning customer").
  • Time awareness: pass the user's local time to the agent, and use simple rules for morning and night suggestions.
  • Recommendation integration: use the recommendation system to get personalized product suggestions for the user.
  • Tone adaptation: detect the user's style (e.g. short messages or casual language) and adjust the response style, within GoCare's brand voice.

items.title: Dependencies
items.text:
• User Profiles & Authentication, User Preferences & Settings, and Conversation Memory Management.
  • Access to order and browsing history.
  • The recommendation system, for personalized product suggestions.

items.title: Risks
items.text:
• Feeling intrusive: too much personal detail can make users uncomfortable.
  • Wrong assumptions: the agent may personalize based on incorrect data.
  • Inconsistent brand voice: adapting tone too much may not fit GoCare's style.
  • More tokens: adding user context to each request increases cost.

items.title: In Scope
items.text:
• Personalized greetings for logged-in users.
  • Using preferences and recent purchases in suggestions.
  • Basic time-of-day awareness (morning and night).

items.title: Out of Scope (for now)
items.text:
• Full user journey tracking.
  • Automatic tone adaptation.
  • Behavior-based adaptation using browsing history.

items.title: 7. Open Questions
items.text: • Which user data is the agent allowed to mention in conversations (e.g. past orders)?

items.title: 8. Assessment
items.text:
In my view, this feature is partly important:

  • Important: suggesting products based on the user's past purchases, such as "Your sunscreen may be running low. Would you like to reorder it?" This directly increases sales.
  • Not important: greeting the user by name and adapting the tone. As in User Profiles & Authentication, what matters is that the agent helps the user find what she wants, not that it says her name.

items.title: Proactive Engagement
items.text: Priority: Medium

items.title: The problem
items.text: Today, the agent only answers when the user writes first. It does not welcome new users, remind users about things they care about, or bring back users who stopped visiting. This means many sales and engagement opportunities are missed.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature lets the agent start useful conversations at the right time:

  • Welcome messages for new users: greet new users and show what the agent can do.
  • Re-engagement messages for inactive users: contact users who have not visited for a while.
  • Proactive product suggestions: suggest products based on the user's interests and history.
  • Timely reminders and notifications: remind users about things like reordering or price drops.
  • Abandoned cart reminders: remind users about products left in their cart.

items.title: Example
items.text:
New user opens the chat: Agent: Welcome to GoCare! 👋 I can help you find products, build a skincare routine, or track your order. What are you looking for today?

Abandoned cart (next day): Agent: You left a vitamin C serum in your cart. It's still available. Would you like to complete your order?

Reorder reminder: Agent: It's been about two months since you bought your sunscreen. Would you like to reorder it?

items.title: 2. Why It Matters
items.text:
• Better first impression: new users quickly understand how to use the agent.
  • Recover lost sales: abandoned cart reminders bring users back to complete orders.
  • Repeat purchases: reorder reminders encourage users to buy again.
  • Bring back inactive users: re-engagement messages reduce customer loss.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Welcome messages: new users receive a welcome message with examples of what the agent can do.
  • FR-02: Re-engagement messages: inactive users receive a message after a set period of inactivity.
  • FR-03: Proactive product suggestions: the agent suggests products based on the user's interests and history.
  • FR-04: Timely reminders and notifications: the agent sends reminders, such as reorder reminders and price drop alerts.
  • FR-05: Abandoned cart reminders: users with items left in the cart receive a reminder.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• User control: users can choose which messages they receive, and can turn them off.
  • Frequency limits: users must not receive too many proactive messages.
  • Privacy & Compliance: messages follow user consent and marketing regulations in Saudi Arabia.
  • Relevance: messages must be useful, not generic spam.

items.title: 4. Technical Approach
items.text:
• Event triggers: define events that start a proactive message, such as first visit, cart left for 24 hours, no visit for 30 days, or time to reorder.
  • Scheduler: a background job checks these conditions and creates messages.
  • Message templates: prepare templates in Arabic and English, personalized with the user's name and products.
  • Delivery channels: messages appear in the chat when the user returns, or are sent as notifications, depending on what GoCare supports.
  • Preferences check: check User Preferences & Settings before sending any message.
  • Recommendation integration: use the recommendation system for proactive product suggestions.
  • Link to other features: coordinate with Churn Prediction and Personalized Marketing in the recommendation roadmap, to avoid sending the same user too many messages from different systems.

items.title: Response Quality Improvements
items.text: Priority: Medium

items.title: The problem
items.text: The agent can answer questions correctly, but its answers are not always easy to read. Some answers are too long, the tone may change from one answer to another, Arabic answers may sound less natural than English ones, and the agent may repeat the same sentences.

items.title: What the feature does
items.text:
The feature improves how the agent's answers look and sound:

  • Response length optimization: short answers for simple questions, and more detail only when needed.
  • Tone and style consistency: the same friendly GoCare voice in every answer.
  • Multilingual response quality: natural, high-quality answers in both Arabic and English.
  • Response formatting: using lists, tables, and emojis where they make answers clearer.
  • Response variation: avoiding repeating the same phrases in every message.

items.title: Example
items.text:
Before:

Thank you for your question. There are many sunscreens available in our store. Sunscreens are important for protecting the skin. Here are some options that you may find suitable for your needs and preferences...

After:

Here are 3 sunscreens for oily skin ☀️

  1. Sunscreen A – SPF 50, oil-free – 85 SAR
  2. Sunscreen B – SPF 50, matte finish – 95 SAR
  3. Sunscreen C – SPF 30, lightweight – 70 SAR

Want me to compare any of them?

items.title: 2. Why It Matters
items.text:
• Easier to read: users find the information they need quickly.
  • Professional brand image: consistent tone reflects GoCare's identity.
  • Better Arabic experience: important for GoCare's Saudi customers.
  • More natural conversations: less repetition makes the agent feel less robotic.

items.title: Functional Requirements
items.text:
• FR-01: Response length optimization: answers match the complexity of the question.
  • FR-02: Tone and style consistency: all answers follow GoCare's voice guidelines.
  • FR-03: Multilingual response quality: Arabic and English answers have the same quality.
  • FR-04: Response formatting: answers use lists, tables, and emojis when helpful.
  • FR-05: Response variation: the agent avoids repeating the same openings and closings.

items.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items.text:
• Readability: answers display correctly in the chat interface, including Arabic right-to-left text.
  • Consistency: formatting rules are applied the same way across all features.
  • Measurability: response quality can be checked with a test set of example questions.

items.title: 4. Technical Approach
items.text:
• Style guide in the system prompt: clear rules for tone, length, formatting, and emoji use, in Arabic and English.
  • Language-specific instructions: separate guidance for natural Arabic, including the preferred dialect or Modern Standard Arabic.
  • Formatting rules: define when to use lists (several products), tables (comparisons), and emojis (light use only).
  • Frontend support: make sure the chat interface renders Markdown, tables, and mixed Arabic and English text correctly.
  • Evaluation set: a set of common questions with expected answer quality, used to test changes before release.
  • Variation: instruct the model to avoid repeated phrases, and review conversation logs for repetitive patterns.

items.title: 5. Dependencies
items.text:
• A GoCare brand voice and style guide.
  • Frontend support for rich formatting.
  • Sample conversations for evaluation.

items.title: 6. Open Questions
items.text:
• Is there an official GoCare brand voice?
  • Does the chat interface support Markdown tables?

items.title: Session Management
items.text: Priority: High · Effort: Medium

items.title: The problem
